\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ممتا} (mamtā)}{ممتا (mamtā)}]{\ur{ممتا} (mamtā) — a mother's love}

\label{lesson:UR-C449-mamta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for eager, then the Urdu for to feel about for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ممتا}}
\textbf{\ur{ممتا}} — \emph{mamtā} — \textquotedblleft{}a mother's love\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{کی} \ur{ممتا} \ur{سب} \ur{سے} \ur{بڑی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ kī mamtā sab se baṛī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A mother's love is the greatest of all.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ممتا}} (\emph{mamtā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{mamatā}, \textquotedblleft{}the feeling of mine\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), built on \emph{mama}, \textquotedblleft{}my\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for a mother's love.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mamtā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mamtā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māṅ kī mamtā sab se baṛī hai.} — A mother's love is the greatest of all.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for eager, then the Urdu for to feel about for, then say \emph{mamtā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ممتا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mother's love\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شفقت} (shafqat)}{شفقت (shafqat)}]{\ur{شفقت} (shafqat) — tender affection (of an elder)}

\label{lesson:UR-C449-shafqat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to feel about for, then the Urdu for a mother's love.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شفقت}}
\textbf{\ur{شفقت}} — \emph{shafqat} — \textquotedblleft{}tender affection (of an elder)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادی} \ur{ہم} \ur{پر} \ur{بڑی} \ur{شفقت} \ur{کرتی} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī ham par baṛī shafqat kartī haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother is very tender with us.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شفقت}} (\emph{shafqat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{shafaqa}, \textquotedblleft{}tenderness, pity\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چومنا} (chūmnā)}{چومنا (chūmnā)}]{\ur{چومنا} (chūmnā) — to kiss}

\label{lesson:UR-C449-chumna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a mother's love, then the Urdu for tender affection.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چومنا}}
\textbf{\ur{چومنا}} — \emph{chūmnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to kiss\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کا} \ur{ماتھا} \ur{چوما۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ ne bachche kā māthā chūmā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother kissed the child's forehead.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{چوما}, \emph{us ne bachche ko chūmā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چومنا}} (\emph{chūmnā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{cúmbati}, \textquotedblleft{}kisses\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4870).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chūmnā}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چمٹنا} (chimaṭnā)}{چمٹنا (chimaṭnā)}]{\ur{چمٹنا} (chimaṭnā) — to cling tightly}

\label{lesson:UR-C449-chimatna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for tender affection, then the Urdu for to kiss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چمٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{چمٹنا}} — \emph{chimaṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to cling tightly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچہ} \ur{ڈر} \ur{کر} \ur{ماں} \ur{سے} \ur{چمٹ} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchā ḍar kar māṅ se chimaṭ gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child took fright and clung to his mother.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{ماں} \ur{سے} \ur{چمٹ} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh māṅ se chimaṭ gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چمٹنا}} (\emph{chimaṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{cimaṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to embrace closely\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{cimb}, \textquotedblleft{}pinch\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 4822).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chimaṭnā}, once more

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عشق} (ishq)}{عشق (ishq)}]{\ur{عشق} (ishq) — passionate love}

\label{lesson:UR-C449-ishq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to kiss, then the Urdu for to cling tightly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عشق}}
\textbf{\ur{عشق}} — \emph{ishq} — \textquotedblleft{}passionate love\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اسے} \ur{موسیقی} \ur{سے} \ur{عشق} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{use mausīqī se ishq hai.}

\begin{quote}
He is passionate about music.

Masculine.

\textbf{\ur{عشق}} (\emph{ishq}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿishq}, \textquotedblleft{}passionate love\textquotedblright{}.

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
